title: API gateway: admission control hook with tier/route classification + feature flags
creator: Rafael Mendes
description:
Goal
Implement a request admission-control hook in the Hosted API gateway that (a) classifies each request into a stable “overload policy key” (tier/route/model/region + streaming vs non-streaming), (b) can be enabled/disabled safely via feature flags, and (c) provides the wiring needed to plug in circuit-breaker decisions from routing/control plane.

This ticket is the edge foundation for the hosted overload protection workstream. The gateway should be able to shed early (before we enqueue work into routing/runtime) once breaker state / capacity signals exist, and do so deterministically with consistent behavior across REST + OpenAI-compatible endpoints.

Scope
- Add an admission-control middleware/hook to the API gateway request path for hosted inference endpoints.
- Request classification:
  - Customer tier (e.g., Free/Pro/Enterprise) based on auth context / plan.
  - Route/model identity (canonical “route_id”/model) across:
    - Redwood native endpoints (e.g., /v1/chat/completions, /v1/embeddings, /v1/rerank)
    - OpenAI-compatible endpoints (same mapping; avoid breaking existing request parsing)
  - Streaming vs non-streaming (important for shed semantics and dashboard breakdowns).
  - Region (gateway region; also include requested region override if present).
- Feature flagging:
  - Global kill switch.
  - Per-region allowlist.
  - Optional per-model or per-route allowlist for canary.
- Define the internal “admission decision” interface: return allow/deny + reason, and emit consistent structured logs + metrics.

Non-goals
- Implementing final customer-facing error mapping/payload shape (tracked in ENG-4823 / ADR-0147).
- Implementing breaker state store in routing (ENG-4824) or capacity signal inputs (ENG-4825).
- Replacing quotas/rate limits.

Implementation notes
1) Classification contract
- Produce a stable key used by downstream breaker evaluation:
  breaker_key := (region, model, route_id, customer_tier, request_kind)
  where request_kind includes {streaming|non_streaming} and possibly {chat|embeddings|rerank}.
- Canonicalize model/route so the same request maps the same way across Redwood-native and OpenAI-compat paths.
- Classification must be best-effort but deterministic:
  - If model is missing/invalid: do not attempt breaker evaluation; fall back to existing validation behavior (400s) handled by existing code path.
  - If tier cannot be determined: default to “unknown” tier and emit metric (classification_unknown_tier_total).

2) Admission control hook
- Middleware runs after auth (so we have tenant/tier), before request is forwarded to routing/control plane.
- Hook interface:
  - Input: request context + breaker_key + request metadata (deadline/timeout, idempotency key if present)
  - Output: allow=true/false, decision_reason (enum), optional retry_after_ms hint (from routing later), and debug metadata.
- For this ticket, implement the plumbing and “no-op allow” behavior behind flag by default:
  - When the flag is disabled, admission hook should run in shadow mode (classify + emit metrics) without denying.

3) Feature flags
- Flag names (initial proposal; keep consistent with rollout plan):
  - overload.admission_control.enabled (global)
  - overload.admission_control.regions (allowlist)
  - overload.admission_control.routes (optional allowlist)
  - overload.admission_control.models (optional allowlist)
- Flags must be hot-reloadable without deploy.
- Add an emergency override path for oncall to disable admission control per-region quickly (admin toggle tracked in INT-1182).

4) Observability
- Metrics (names are placeholders; final naming reviewed in ENG-4829 / observability standard):
  - gateway_admission_evaluations_total{region, tier, route_id, model, streaming}
  - gateway_admission_denied_total{region, tier, route_id, model, streaming, reason}
  - gateway_request_classification_errors_total{type}
  - gateway_admission_shadow_denies_total{reason} (if we support “shadow deny” evaluation during canary)
- Logs/traces:
  - Add structured log field admission.classification_key and admission.decision (allow/deny/shadow_deny).
  - Attach trace span “admission_control” with attributes region/tier/route_id/model/streaming (avoid high-cardinality values beyond allowed set).

5) Compatibility constraints
- Must not change existing behavior when disabled:
  - No new 4xx/5xx codes.
  - No new headers visible to customers (internal headers must be stripped).
- Ensure OpenAI-compatible requests are classified correctly even when model name is provided in different places (body vs path vs header); if ambiguous, prefer the existing routing resolution order.

Acceptance criteria
- [x] Middleware exists and is wired into hosted gateway request path.
- [x] Deterministic classification implemented for tier/route/model/streaming/region; validated with unit tests for:
  - Redwood native chat/completions
  - OpenAI-compat chat/completions
  - embeddings
  - rerank
- [x] Feature flags implemented (global + per-region) and default OFF.
- [x] Metrics emitted for evaluations and classification errors; verified in staging.
- [x] Shadow-mode path does not affect responses and adds <1ms median overhead in staging perf spot check.
- [x] Link to follow-up work: once routing breaker evaluation is ready, replace no-op allow with routing call and pass through deny reason (ENG-4824/ENG-4825).

Risks / mitigations
- Cardinality blowups: do not include raw tenant_id in metric labels; tier should be a small enum. Model should be canonical model ID (bounded set), not arbitrary user input.
- Misclassification causing unfairness: keep classification logic centralized and test against representative requests; add explicit “unknown” buckets + alerting if unknown spikes.
- Flag safety: ensure the kill switch is evaluated before any deny path.

Links
- Initiative umbrella: ENG-4821
- Error semantics ADR: adr-0147-overload-error-taxonomy-and-http-mapping (tracked via ENG-4823)
- Circuit breaker state model ADR: adr-0148-circuit-breaker-state-model-and-hysteresis
- Related PR (gateway middleware + admission hook scaffolding): sources/github/redwood/pr-18421.json

Progress updates
- 2025-10-16 (Amara): Drafted classification table for hosted endpoints + OpenAI-compat mapping. Added initial route_id canonicalization helper; pending review from Brian Murphy (compat).
- 2025-10-21 (Rafael): Please ensure tier is derived from auth/plan object and not inferred from API key prefix. Add “unknown_tier” metric so we can detect auth propagation bugs.
- 2025-10-24 (Brian): OpenAI-compat note: model can appear in body for chat/completions; keep existing precedence order and only classify after request parsing to avoid divergence.
- 2025-10-29 (Amara): Implemented middleware in shadow-mode. Flags wired (global + per-region). Added unit tests for chat/completions + embeddings. Perf spot check in staging looks OK (<1ms median added, p99 unchanged within noise).
- 2025-11-03 (Sergio Costa): Metrics naming needs to follow the standard; ok to land placeholders but please coordinate with ENG-4829 before dashboard work.
- 2025-11-06 (Amara): Merged. Default OFF. Shadow metrics visible in staging. Follow-ups: (1) swap placeholder metrics to final names once observability standard lands, (2) add rerank classification tests, (3) integrate routing breaker evaluation call once ENG-4824 is ready.

Follow-ups
- Add rerank endpoint classification tests (small gap; create a sub-task if needed).
- Replace placeholder metrics naming with standardized names (ENG-4829).
- Wire admission hook to routing breaker evaluation API (ENG-4824/ENG-4825).
